t: Longest Balanced Substring After One Swap — Prefix Balance + Hash Map
o: A balanced substring has equal 0s and 1s. Using balance b = (#1 - #0) prefix sums, a substring is balanced iff its balance is 0. One swap changes a window's balance by at most 1 (exactly one of the swapped characters may lie inside), so: even-length windows must already have balance 0; odd-length windows with balance ±1 can be fixed by swapping an inside majority character with an opposite character outside — possible iff the string contains more of that minority character than the window does. Track earliest prefix positions in a hash map for O(n).
k: Balance-0 windows are directly balanced; the longest is found via earliest-occurrence of each prefix value.
Odd windows with balance +1 need an external '0' (total zeros > zeros inside); balance -1 needs an external '1'.
Both cases reduce to looking up pre[j] and pre[j]±1 in a 'first occurrence' map.

a.n: Approach 1: Quadratic Scan with Prefix Balances
a.i: Compute prefix balances once, then examine every (i, j) pair: balance 0 → candidate; balance ±1 with odd length → candidate if the needed outside character exists.
s: For each i < j compute b = pre[j] - pre[i], L = j - i.
If b == 0 update answer with L.
If |b| == 1 and L odd, check the outside-character condition and update.

a.i: For each j, the longest window ending at j with balance b starts at the first index with prefix value pre[j] - b. Query b = 0, +1, -1 in one map, validating the ±1 cases with the outside-character counts.
s: Build pre and totals tz, to.
For j = 1..n: for b in {0, 1, -1}, look up first[pre[j] - b]; for b=0 take the length; for b=±1 take odd lengths satisfying the outside-character condition.
Insert pre[j] into the map if absent.
a.t: O(n) — one pass with O(1) hash operations
a.sp: O(n) — prefix array and hash map

w: Present the hash-map solution; the quadratic version is only a stepping stone. Pitfalls: querying the map before inserting the current prefix (otherwise zero-length windows appear), the parity requirement for ±1 windows (balance ±1 forces odd length), and verifying the swap partner actually exists outside the window (Example 2: '111' has no zeros at all, so nothing helps and the answer is 0). Follow-up: allow k swaps (sliding window over balance with a small DP).
